stage_a.note: Founder is smiling, energetic, and highly positive while demonstrating the product.
Strong engagement and excitement when discussing the app and analytics.
Friendly and professional greeting to the sharks, maintaining a courteous demeanor.

venture.description: A portable cable resistance fitness machine that replaces bulky gym equipment and connects to a coaching app.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar introduces MaxPro, a portable, connected cable resistance machine offering 5 to 300 pounds of resistance, and asks for $500k.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks to confirm if the weight can be adjusted from 3 to 300 pounds.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar confirms and invites Robert to come up and try flexing his muscles on the machine.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert agrees to try the machine and walks up to the stage.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks what weight is currently set on the machine she is looking at.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar explains that the cables are 10 feet long and made of Dyneema, a high-strength material.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks Nezar what weight is currently set for him to pull.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar tells Robert that the weight is currently set to just 5 pounds.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert jokes that he thinks the weight is actually 7 pounds, making the panel laugh.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar steps in to help Robert adjust the machine and shows him how to use it.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert pulls the cables on the machine to test the resistance.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks Nezar if the weight he is pulling is 50 pounds.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar answers that it is level 12, which equates to about 45 pounds of resistance.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert expresses amazement that all of the resistance is generated from the small device.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin notes the $20 million valuation and asks for the company's history, start date, and year-over-year sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar explains that product development took over five years, and they first started shipping in July of last year.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks how much they did in sales last year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar states that they made 4 million dollars in sales last year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks what they have done in sales so far this year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar answers that they have done over 8 million dollars in sales this year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori expresses dislike for resistance bands due to the hassle of mounting them on doors, asking about exercise versatility.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar explains the product's versatility, showing how it mounts to doors, a specialized wall track, trees, or fences.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks Nezar how he came up with the idea and what his professional background is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar states that his primary background is in the automotive industry, where he spent 25 years.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks Nezar if he is an engineer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar confirms that he is an engineer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if he is a mechanical engineer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar confirms and explains he traveled overseas frequently and wanted to figure out how to get resistance workouts on the road.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks for the cost to make the product, the selling price, and the cost of the app.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar states that the retail value of the product is $849.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks to confirm the high retail price of $849.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar explains the landed cost is $205, plus $20 total for pick, pack, and shipping.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they sell direct-to-consumer only.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar confirms that 97% of their sales are direct-to-consumer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks how they are managing to sell $8 million worth of the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar credits Covid and spending a ton of money on marketing for their high sales.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks what their monthly cash burn is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar states that their essential burn rate is about $100,000 per month.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they could become profitable if they slowed down their marketing spend.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar answers that it is a yes and a no, explaining that they make money on every unit but reinvest it.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin challenges Nezar's answer, stating that it has to be one or the other.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar clarifies that they are profitable on a unit basis, but they take all the money to reinvest.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond acknowledges that he understands the business strategy in a highly competitive market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar volunteers that they currently have over 3,000 daily active users on their app.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert recaps the previous year's sales of 4 million dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar confirms the 4 million sales figure.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks how much money they made on the 4 million in sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar states that they made just over $50,000.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks if they will make or lose money on the projected 8 million in sales this year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar predicts they will likely reach over 12 million in sales this year instead.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks what profit they will make on those projected sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar estimates they will be close to breaking even, possibly losing around $100,000.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark points out that to scale, they must invest, asking how they plan to fund the growth.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar reveals they took a revenue-based line of credit to fund the growth.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks what percentage they have to pay out for every dollar lent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar answers that the rate started at 20%, went to 25%, and is now 28%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar volunteers that they currently have over 5 million dollars in inventory.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks for confirmation of the 5 million inventory figure.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori questions why they hold so much inventory when required to do certain quantities.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar explains it was a judgment call because they had just signed an endorsement deal with Shaq.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks about the specifics of the equity deal with Shaq.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar states that Shaq earns his equity over four years.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks how much equity Shaq actually earns.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar clarifies that Shaq gets 1.25% this year and it can go up to 5%.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark points out the tough spot the company is in, needing ad money to blow out inventory for the holidays.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar agrees, stating he needs the expertise of the Sharks to help.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond offers the $500k with a $25 per unit royalty until recouped, which then converts to 4% equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar clarifies if he heard the word royalty in the offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond confirms the royalty and repeats the terms of his offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks what specific help he needs from a Shark.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar explains that Sharks know how to open doors in retail, hotels, and the military.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond presses Nezar for feedback on the half-million-dollar offer standing before him.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar replies that he was thinking about Daymond the whole time.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks Nezar what he thinks about the offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks what their return rate is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar answers that the return rate is less than 5%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar points out that a less than 5% return rate is really good in consumer goods.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark tells Nezar he is overselling at this point.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond complains that he has been sitting for 20 minutes waiting for an answer to his offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks if they really need the app and all the rest of the connected features.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar defends the app, stating everything has an app today and they are building a new one from scratch.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they are losing a ton of money on the app right now.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how much money they could save if they didn't have the app.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar emphasizes that the app isn't just a connection, it displays how the user is working out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin cites a philosophical disagreement on spending money on an app when others exist, and exits.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks if Nezar became more valuable and says he wants to see if he can get to an offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark offers $500k for 3% equity, plus an additional 5% in advisory shares vesting the same way as Shaq's.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert states that Mark's offer is far more generous than what he would make, and exits.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark playfully asks Nezar if he became even more valuable after that.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar turns to Daymond and asks if he answered all of his questions.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark interrupts, telling Nezar there are no more questions and he has to decide.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori says Mark's offer is really good and she is going to go out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar tells Mark he appreciates the offer but wants to ask him one question.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond tells Nezar he better make sure the question is good because he is out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar reacts with surprise to Daymond exiting the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar asks Mark if there is a way they can replace the line of credit.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark answers potentially, but refuses to commit to it right now.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin reminds Nezar that the only offer he has left is Mark's.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Nezar accepts Mark's offer, stating he is all in.

decisions.terms: $500k for 4% stake + a royalty of $25 per unit sold until investment is recouped
decisions.note: Offers $500k with a $25 per unit royalty until recouped, then 4% equity.
Philosophical disagreement on spending money on the app.

decisions.terms: $500k for a 3% stake + up to 5% in advisory shares that vests over time
decisions.note: Offers $500k for 3% equity, plus up to 5% in advisory shares.
Mark's offer is far more generous than he would make.
Mark offered a really good deal.

decisions.terms: Absolutely Mark, dude, I'm all in.
